clue.text: Each one dropped a type of anesthetic

indicators.note: something dropped is let fall and left behind, so a letter goes missing from the word

blocks.note: 'either' can mean each, as in trees on either side of the road
the Roman numeral for one, the letter that is taken away

explanation.surface: A doctor gives every patient one dose, and each of them drops off under a particular anesthetic.
explanation.walkthrough: EITHER loses its I to leave ETHER. The sense of either as 'each' (on either bank) is the step most solvers miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was one of the earliest general anesthetics, inhaled to put surgical patients to sleep.

clue.text: Gives a job to spy and mole, irresponsibly

indicators.note: acting irresponsibly means behaving carelessly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An intelligence agency carelessly hires a spy who turns out to be a mole.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ someone is to hire them, paying them to do work.

clue.text: Improve clumsy boy MC's arrangement of "Beeswax"

indicators.note: something clumsy is awkwardly put together, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: to hone a skill is to sharpen or improve it
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A rapper tries to polish a clumsy young MC's version of a song titled "Beeswax".
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks dress Beeswax up as a song title; the definition is the material itself, arranged in cells.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees build honeycomb as a lattice of hexagonal wax cells, so it is the way their wax is laid out.

clue.text: Torment a lamb, in part

blocks.note: first meaning: to cause great pain, as on the old instrument of torture
second meaning: a cut of meat from the ribs of a lamb

explanation.walkthrough: 'In part' looks like a signal to find letters inside 'Torment a lamb'; it marks a cut of the animal. A rack of lamb is a joint of ribs.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack is both a torture frame, hence to torment, and a butcher's rib joint, as in rack of lamb.

clue.text: Once again, go through irate letters — some of them more than once

indicators.note: only the letters of the angry word are wanted, free to be used in any order

blocks.note: taken as written

blocks.clueFragment: some of them more than once
blocks.note: R and T are each used a second time, and E twice more

explanation.surface: Someone rereads some furious correspondence, going over several of the angry letters again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: REITERATE uses only the five letters of IRATE: R and T appear twice and E three times, so the solver must reuse some letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To reiterate is to say or do something over again, repeating a statement already made.

clue.text: In the military, time off before operation gets one a little water

indicators.note: the leave period gets, that is takes in, an extra letter among its own

blocks.note: R and R, rest and recuperation, is military slang for leave
the Roman numeral for one
the usual abbreviation for an operation

explanation.surface: A soldier's leave before a mission comes with just a sprinkle of water.
explanation.walkthrough: R AND R takes I after its first A, giving RA-I-NDR, then OP follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A raindrop is a single small drop of rain falling from a cloud.

clue.text: Where to find this woman's name?

definitions.text: Where to find this woman's name?

blocks.clueFragment: Where to find this woman's name?
blocks.note: surface reading: a question about where a woman's name might be recorded, a register or directory

blocks.clueFragment: Where to find this woman's name?
blocks.note: setter's reading: split the name in two and it says where you are writing it right now, among the squares

explanation.walkthrough: INGRID splits as IN GRID: the woman's name is found in the crossword grid you are filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid is a woman's given name, made famous by the actress Ingrid Bergman.

clue.text: Listening to a Japanese teenager, possibly putting someone out of their misery

definitions.text: putting someone out of their misery

indicators.note: listening means taking in by ear, so the words are judged by their sound

blocks.note: a Japanese teenager is an example of a young person living in Asia

explanation.surface: Having to listen to a Japanese teenager is the kind of ordeal you would like to be rescued from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' signals that a Japanese teen is just one example of a youth in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Euthanasia is the deliberate ending of a life to relieve incurable suffering.

clue.text: A dog and a car

blocks.note: taken as written
a cur is a mongrel dog
taken as written

explanation.surface: A simple list of possessions: a dog and a car.
explanation.walkthrough: Acura is the luxury car brand that Honda sells in North America.
explanation.definitionFit: Acura is a make of car, so any of its models is an automobile.

clue.text: Enclose amber waves outside of Cheyenne

indicators.note: waves move to and fro, so the letters are tossed into a new order
the outside of a word is its two ends, so only the first and last letters count

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters of the Wyoming city

explanation.surface: A patriotic picture: amber waves of grain enclosing Cheyenne, borrowing from "America the Beautiful".
explanation.walkthrough: "Amber waves of grain" is a line from the song America the Beautiful, which makes 'waves' read as a noun rather than a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace is to hold in the arms, so to surround or include something.

clue.text: Preparing for a trip around the outskirts of Nagasaki in a state of extreme fear

definitions.text: in a state of extreme fear

indicators.note: the outskirts of a town are its edges, so only the first and last letters of the place are kept
one word goes around the other, wrapping it on both sides

blocks.note: filling a suitcase before travelling
the first and last letters of the Japanese city

explanation.surface: A traveller frantically packs for a trip to the edge of Nagasaki, terrified the whole time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preparing for a trip' sounds like the definition of the whole answer, but it is only the outer word; the definition is the fear at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone panicking is gripped by sudden terror that overwhelms clear thinking.

clue.text: Hitch drone bomber at first behind rear of aircraft

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its tail end, so its last letter is kept
at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: the last letter of aircraft
a drone is a low continuous hum
the first letter of bomber

explanation.surface: A military scene: a drone and a bomber hitched up behind the tail of another aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drone' looks like an unmanned aircraft in this setting; here it is the noise. 'Behind' only places the first letter before the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To thumb a ride is to hitchhike, signalling drivers with a raised thumb.

clue.text: Antelope decapitated — gory times!

indicators.note: losing its head means the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written, before its head is removed
x is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A headless antelope: grim, bloody days on the savannah.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decapitated' seems to describe the antelope, but it acts on the word that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: The oryx is a large straight-horned antelope of African and Arabian deserts.

clue.text: Capital spot, said to be shifted two degrees

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the words count by their sound and not their spelling
letters that have been shifted are moved out of place into a new order

blocks.note: a spot is an ad, a short commercial, and to be gives is
AA, Associate of Arts, and BBA, Bachelor of Business Administration, two American degrees

explanation.surface: A capital is said to have moved two degrees on the map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' is a TV or radio commercial slot. AA and BBA are standard US college degrees; their five letters are rearranged into ABABA.
explanation.definitionFit: Addis Ababa is the capital city of Ethiopia.

clue.text: Asked to place particle inside D

indicators.note: one piece is set inside another, sitting among the outer word's letters

blocks.note: the lone capital letter, read as a petite D, that is a small one
an ion is a charged atomic particle

explanation.surface: A physics instruction: you are asked to put a particle into a box labelled D.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter D has to be described in words: a little D is a petite D. The particle goes in after PETIT, giving PETIT-ION-E-D.
explanation.definitionFit: To petition is to make a formal request, so someone who petitioned asked for something.

clue.text: Inside and out, put an end to chef's workspace

indicators.note: one word sits inside while another stays out around it, both from the same phrase

blocks.note: to put an end to something is to halt it; this is the outer word
to put an end to a plan is also to forbid it; this is the inner word

explanation.surface: A health inspector orders that a kitchen's cooking area be shut down entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: The one phrase is used twice, once for each meaning: one word to halt, one word to forbid, the second sitting inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A stovetop is the cooking surface with burners on top of a range, where a cook works.

clue.text: Injure fellow with broken leg

indicators.note: something broken is smashed out of shape, so the word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a fellow is a man
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A man has been hurt and has a broken leg to show for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To mangle is to badly damage or mutilate by crushing or tearing.

clue.text: Eviscerate front of book stuck in malfunctioning green printer

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter
a device that malfunctions works out of order, so the letters are scrambled
something stuck in another thing is lodged inside it

blocks.note: to gut an animal is to remove its innards
the first letter of book
taken as written, then rearranged around the single letter

explanation.surface: Someone tears the cover off a book jammed in a broken eco-friendly printer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Printer' looks like the office machine; it is the man who printed the first European Bible with movable type.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Gutenberg introduced movable-type printing to Europe in the fifteenth century.

clue.text: Slandered monstrous devil, assuming I was taken in

indicators.note: something taken in is admitted inside, so the extra letters go among the others
monstrous suggests something deformed, so the letters are twisted out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
if means on the assumption that
taken as written

explanation.surface: A demon is defamed, and the narrator confesses to being fooled by it.
explanation.walkthrough: IF and I join the letters of DEVIL, and all eight are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: To vilify someone is to speak of them abusively, blackening their name.

clue.text: Shy bride undressed in mix-up?

indicators.note: stripping off the outer layer leaves only what lies inside the phrase

blocks.note: the letters inside, once the first and last are stripped away

explanation.surface: A bashful bride, caught half-dressed in some wedding-day confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the S of Shy and the E of bride and the remaining run of letters is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid is a cross or blend of two kinds, so a mixture of different things.

clue.text: Vicious, nasty fault, eh?

indicators.note: a nasty mess is a jumble, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks, with a shrug, whether a cruel and unpleasant flaw is really so bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hateful is malicious and spiteful, full of cruelty toward others.

clue.text: Form of address, outside-in, for government official

indicators.note: one word stays on the outside, wrapping around the short word attached to it

blocks.note: the polite title used before a man's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: Etiquette advice: a reversed way of addressing someone suits a senior civil servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside-in' looks like one adjective meaning inverted; split it, and the polite title goes outside the word in: MI-N-ISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister is a member of government in charge of a department, such as a cabinet officer.

clue.text: Dad, when parting, takes five meals

indicators.note: one word parts another, splitting it so it sits in the middle

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
to take five is to take a short break

explanation.surface: Father, on leaving, takes five meals with him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes five' looks like a count of meals; it is the idiom for a break. PA splits it: RE-PA-STS.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal word for a meal, so repasts are meals.

clue.text: Parent of a lepidopterist?

blocks.note: first meaning: a female parent
second meaning, read whimsically: someone who studies or hunts moths

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as MOTH-ER, one who deals in moths, on the pattern of baker or hunter; the question mark flags that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A lepidopterist studies butterflies and moths, so a moth collector fits the playful second sense.

clue.text: To speaker's helper, holding back stogie is kind of sad and kind of funny

definitions.text: kind of sad and kind of funny

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from its end to its start
one word holds another, keeping it between its letters

blocks.note: taken as written
a stogie is a cheap cigar
a microphone helps a speaker be heard

explanation.surface: Someone handing a cigar to the speaker's assistant finds the whole scene bittersweet and comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker's helper' looks like an aide or assistant; it is the device a speaker talks into.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragicomic describes something blending tragedy and comedy, both mournful and amusing.

clue.text: Cube coated with gold is so long

indicators.note: a coating covers something on all sides, so one word wraps around another

blocks.note: a die is a numbered cube used in games
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A gilded cube is described as being so long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So long' looks like a measurement of the cube, but it is the farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is French for goodbye, as is the informal farewell so long.

clue.text: Contrarian attaches clip

indicators.note: a contrarian goes the opposite way, so the word runs in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to pin is to fasten one thing to another

explanation.surface: A difficult person fastens things with a paper clip just to be awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrarian' reads like a noun for the person doing the attaching, but it only signals the turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: To snip is to cut with small quick strokes of scissors, the same as to clip.

clue.text: Leaders of the House undermine society this way

indicators.note: the leaders of a group are those at the front, so the first letters are taken

blocks.note: the first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Political commentary: the heads of the House of Representatives are eroding society in this manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus means in this manner, as in 'do it thus'.

clue.text: Pretend to hide returning soldier in swamp

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word is read in the opposite direction
a hiding place keeps something inside it, so one word goes into another

blocks.note: GI is the usual term for an American soldier
a fen is low marshy ground

explanation.surface: A soldier coming home pretends to lie low in a swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: GI, short for 'government issue', is the standard nickname for an American soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: To feign is to put on a false show of something, such as illness or interest.

clue.text: Raises chickens, catches 8

indicators.note: whatever is caught is held, so one word is gripped inside the other

blocks.note: female chickens
the numeral written out as a word

explanation.surface: A farmer keeps poultry, and the birds catch something numbered 8.
explanation.walkthrough: The 8 looks like a cross-reference to 8-down, but it is simply the number spelt out, held inside HENS.
explanation.definitionFit: To heighten something is to make it higher or more intense, so heightens means lifts or increases.

clue.text: Cleaned up city governed by Mayor Koch

blocks.note: Los Angeles, usually shortened to LA
a place governed by someone is under them
Ed Koch was mayor of New York City from 1978 to 1989

explanation.surface: New York was cleaned up while Mayor Koch ran it, a familiar political boast.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to New York, but the city wanted is LA, placed under Koch's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundered means washed, and also describes illicit money made to look clean.

clue.text: Expresses frustration with sung mass

indicators.note: a word that is sung is heard rather than read, so its sound matters, not its spelling

blocks.note: mass and size both describe how big something is

explanation.surface: A churchgoer grumbles about having to sit through a long choral Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like a church service, given 'sung', but it means bulk.
explanation.definitionFit: A sigh is a long audible breath that signals weariness or exasperation.
